questions.prompt: Each device of a pair has \(\mu_nC_{ox}W/L = 2\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\) and \(V_T = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\); the tail carries 0.4 mA and needs at least 0.3 V across it. Find the lowest input common-mode voltage (V).
questions.explanation: Each side carries 0.2 mA, so \(V_{ov} = \sqrt{0.4/2} = 0.447\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{GS} = 0.947\ \mathrm{V}\). The common source must stay at 0.3 V or more, so \(V_{CM} \ge 1.25\ \mathrm{V}\).

questions.prompt: What does the pair's large-signal transfer curve \(I_{D1} - I_{D2}\) versus \(v_{id}\) look like?
options: A straight line for all inputs
Linear near zero, then bending and saturating at \(\pm I_{SS}\)
A parabola with its minimum at zero
questions.explanation: The tail fixes the sum, so the difference can never exceed \(I_{SS}\) (reader Sec. 16.4).
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

questions.prompt: A pair is balanced at \(V_{ov} = 0.25\ \mathrm{V}\) per device. At what \(|v_{id}|\) (mV) does one device turn off completely?
questions.explanation: Full steering puts \(I_{SS}\) in one device, whose overdrive becomes \(\sqrt2V_{ov}\) while the other sits at 0: \(|v_{id}| = \sqrt2(0.25) = 354\ \mathrm{mV}\).
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

questions.prompt: A pair has \(I_{SS} = 0.4\ \mathrm{mA}\) and \(V_{ov} = 0.25\ \mathrm{V}\) at balance (\(r_o\) ignored). Find \(I_{D1} - I_{D2}\) in µA for \(v_{id} = 100\ \mathrm{mV}\).
questions.explanation: With \(\mu_nC_{ox}W/L = I_{SS}/V_{ov}^2 = 6.4\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\): \(\Delta I = \tfrac12(6.4\ \mathrm{m})(0.1)\sqrt{4(0.4\ \mathrm{m})/6.4\ \mathrm{m} - 0.01} = 157\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). The linear estimate \(g_mv_{id} = 160\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) is 2% high.
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

questions.prompt: For small \(v_{id}\), the slope of \(I_{D1} - I_{D2}\) is \(g_m\) of one device. What is it in terms of the tail current?
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

questions.prompt: A pair has \(V_{DD} = 1.8\ \mathrm{V}\), \(I_{SS} = 0.3\ \mathrm{mA}\) and \(R_D = 4\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). With the input fully steered, what is the lower drain voltage (V)?
questions.explanation: All of \(I_{SS}\) flows on one side: \(1.8 - 0.3(4) = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\); the other drain rises to 1.8 V.

questions.prompt: At fixed \(I_{SS}\), you make the devices narrower so \(V_{ov}\) rises. What happens?
options: The linear input range widens, but \(g_m\) falls
questions.explanation: Range \(\propto V_{ov}\) and \(g_m = I_{SS}/V_{ov}\): the linearity-gain trade-off.
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

questions.prompt: A pair has \(V_{DD} = 1.8\ \mathrm{V}\), \(I_{SS} = 0.4\ \mathrm{mA}\), \(R_D = 3\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) and \(V_T = 0.45\ \mathrm{V}\). What is the highest input common-mode voltage (V) that keeps the input devices saturated at balance?
questions.explanation: The drains sit at \(1.8 - 0.2(3) = 1.2\ \mathrm{V}\). Saturation needs \(V_D \ge V_G - V_T\), so \(V_{CM} \le 1.2 + 0.45 = 1.65\ \mathrm{V}\).

questions.prompt: A pair is biased with \(I_{SS} = 0.5\ \mathrm{mA}\) at \(V_{ov} = 0.25\ \mathrm{V}\). Find each device's \(g_m\) in mS.
questions.explanation: \(g_m = 2(0.25\ \mathrm{mA})/0.25 = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\). Using the full tail current gives 4 mS.
questions.figure_alt: Differential pair large-signal transfer: the current difference (I_D1 - I_D2)/I_SS versus v_id is linear near zero and saturates at plus or minus 1 once one device cuts off, at v_id = plus or minus sqrt(2) V_ov.

options: Split the inputs into differential and common-mode parts and solve one half circuit for each
Always with the full large-signal equations
As a single CS stage with both inputs added
questions.explanation: Symmetry lets each mode be solved on half the circuit.
